context:
Real-world datasets test real-life data types (timestamps, geo coordinates, nested string categoricals) and skew characteristics differing from synthetic TPC generators. Required scope is 15 bundles (9 NYC Taxi, 6 Flight Data at SF 0.1 and 1.0) plus up to 3 conditional FlightData SF 10 bundles.

Revalidated 2026-10-01. Query counts match the loaded classes (25 and 20). Both suites are rows of the 84-cell live-cloud corpus campaign, so progress is read from that campaign's per-cell table. The campaign's interim policy is to run FlightData on cloud at SF 1 and SF 5 and to hold SF 10 until the source decision exists. The BigQuery and Snowflake FlightData SF 10 bundles on disk carry identity, replacement and timing holds. Runs inside the campaign's limits (6 h per cell, BigQuery cap from 2026-09-22) need no new approval; anything else needs one stating command, maximum runtime, log path and stop condition.
description:
Expand live cloud benchmark runs across BigQuery, Databricks, and Snowflake to the Real-World domain benchmark suites:
- NYC Taxi: 25 OLAP queries on taxi trip data covering temporal, geographic, and fare analysis (SF 0.1, 1.0, 10.0)
- Flight Data: 20 OLAP queries on airline on-time performance and delay metrics (SF 0.1, 1.0 required; SF 10.0 only if the source policy allows it)

FlightData downloads monthly BTS archives, and 1990-01..1999-12 and part of 1987 are unavailable, so only 327 of the 410 months SF 10 requests can be supplied. SF 10 is gated on the decision recorded by flightdata-source-status-and-alternatives (real months only, a capped scale, or another source).

Execute across all three cloud platforms. Verify 100% query execution and validate resulting bundles against repository gates.
